name: Weeks
overview: The Bible reveals that a week is primarily a period of seven days, as seen in Genesis 2:2 where God rested on the seventh day after creation. Weeks also represent longer periods, such as seven years, illustrated in Genesis 29:27-28 with Jacob fulfilling a week of service. The counting of weeks is foundational to biblical timekeeping, culminating in the Feast of Weeks or Pentecost, a celebration tied to the harvest and marked by counting seven sabbaths plus one day to reach fifty days, as described in Leviticus 23:15-16 and Exodus 34:22. This demonstrates how weeks serve both practical and spiritual purposes in Scripture.
